title: Visible high-drop experiments with accepted physical time; material accuracy and realtime remain open
changes: Coupled lab adds Target view, Follow ball and Full drop with actual-position markers, simulated time, gap and speed. Run 10 steps shows its duration; Run to ball contact advances accepted steps with Stop. Edited settings are applied before Run and support motion cannot masquerade as ball contact. The exact replay log has a larger bounded storage allowance. Physics laws and gates are unchanged.

Coupled GPU lab adds Linear solve: Resident cuSOLVER on pinned Windows x64. Reusable buffers and device error status support actual changed-input command replay. Eight tested glass/oak/iron/ice histories match CuPy reference exactly. CuPy reference remains default; the full nonlinear loop is still host controlled and realtime remains open.

Coupled GPU lab tries the full Newton step first, then batches smaller choices on CUDA. Select Step-size probes to compare the retained one-at-a-time reference. Four-material accepted poses, velocities, material history and work records match exactly. Measured low-energy wall time improves 12–26%; full material accuracy and realtime remain open.

Ball / ground timing control uses explicit material/mass-derived contact refinement. Compare Before, actual accepted peak-impact microstep and Live. The derivative scale resolves microsecond contact positions. Connected sheets at refined contact phases still stop at the bounded trial budget; Reference remains their default. No whole-world realtime or material fracture qualification.

Coupled lab adds ranked Newton starting guesses and an explicit single-start reference. The same total 24-iteration bound and physical gates remain. Strong glass/oak/iron/ice controls now finish at both tested timesteps; trajectory differences remain substantial. Run 0.1 s displays actual accepted states.

Coupled CUDA fault collection now runs in parallel with unchanged fault priority and physical sums. The lab shows rejected-trial counts and rollback; its log records actual failed Newton inputs/candidates/Jacobian. Strong glass/ice convergence remains unresolved.

Coupled 3D lab now defaults to Parallel CUDA and offers Serial reference. Ordered material/contact contributions and current-Jacobian reuse preserve all four tested physical histories exactly. Controlled runs improve to about 1.4–3.0 wall seconds per 0.042 physical seconds; still far from realtime.

New /coupled 3D page: nine connected finite cells, density-derived ball, fixed supports, actual CUDA material/contact/body solve, Before/Live and downloadable complete microstep records. Low-energy four-material controls pass; fracture/yield and realtime remain unqualified.

GPU material inspector now shows actual CUDA force directions and body force/torque pairs. General finite-frame reactions use the same CPU/CUDA energy gradient; normal controlled loading has zero torque. The diagram still has no dynamics clock.

GPU material laws at /materials runs persistent damage and six-mode plastic return from shared C++ source via CuPy. Apply a common opening, unload and inspect retained history. Controlled constitutive loading only, not dynamic GPU fracture or dents.

PhysX reuses resident CUDA pose/velocity buffers. Every substep is retained; all 15360 refined stack states match the independent column reference exactly. The slower column path remains available in the profiler.
GPU lab shows actual SDK stepping, GPU observation and host audit time. Every calculated substep remains recorded; constitutive port is separate from this rigid solver.
GPU solver now compares Newton XPBD and PhysX TGS in the same 3D world. Stack control uses zero bounce/friction and 1/1920 s; glass/oak/iron/ice complete in scoped controls.
PhysX records actual CUDA poses, mass/inertia and normal contact impulses each substep. Friction and full contact/numerical work are not yet in that account; no bonded GPU fracture or dents.
Open GPU contact yard: CUDA-calculated ball drops, two-body impacts and free fall. CPU material lab remains available; no GPU fracture or dents yet.
GPU frames use actual resident Newton/Warp states, with every substep recorded. The full 27-block stack stops at an energy refusal and retains its last accepted scene.
Optional Contact response → Coupled friction + bounce solves sliding and twist together while retaining native material restitution. Reference stays default.
Physics step selects the actual 1/960 or refined 1/1920 s experiment. Before/Live shows original and accepted native geometry.

The reproduced refined glass refusal is twisting friction adding energy in the direction of existing spin. Terminal rejected records now retain original-cell impulses and actual force/solver velocities.
Glass/oak/iron/ice complete at both timesteps in the initial trial. Full convergence, large energy deficits, connected calculation speed and thermal/fluid/power laws remain unfinished.
